parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of SettleClaim fits the application layer. It loads the claim through a repository, gets coverage terms through an application port, calls the domain methods (claim.decline, claim.settle) and saves the result. The problem is the method signature `settle(claimId: string, request?: Request)`, which takes an express `Request`. Handling HTTP requests is a transport concern, which belongs to the presentation layer (src/*/api). Because of this parameter, the use case's public contract knows about the web framework, and the use case can't be called cleanly from non-HTTP entry points. The parameter is never used, so no transport logic actually runs. Even so, accepting the framework request object is a presentation responsibility in an application file. The import of express on its own is an import-direction issue and out of scope. This finding is about the transport-aware method contract.

violations.message: SettleClaim.settle(claimId, request?: Request) takes an express HTTP Request in its signature. Accepting a transport request is a presentation-layer (api) responsibility. The controller should map the request to plain inputs before it calls the use case.
